title: New Phase 2 REC-4881 Data Presented at CGA-IGC Show Deep, Durable Polyp Burden Reductions in FAP, with Activity Across the GI Tract and in Larger, Higher-Risk Polyps
content: New Phase 2 REC-4881 Data Presented at CGA-IGC Show Deep, Durable Polyp Burden Reductions in FAP, with Activity Across the GI Tract and in Larger, Higher-Risk Polyps November 2, 2026 at 4:25 PM EST PDF Version Updated TUPELO results featured in a Presidential Plenary at CGA-IGC : Lisa Boardman , M.D., Professor of Medicine at Mayo Clinic , presented updated findings from the Phase 1b/2 TUPELO trial in familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) at the Collaborative Group of the Americas on Inherited Gastrointestinal Cancer (CGA-IGC) Annual Meeting. Deep reductions sustained off treatment: In an expanded adult population aged 18 years and older, after 12 weeks of treatment, patients achieved a 47% median reduction in total polyp burden, with approximately 1 in 3 achieving reductions of ≥65%. Twelve weeks after stopping treatment, 85% of evaluable patients remained below baseline. Activity throughout the upper and lower GI tract, including near-clearance : After 12 weeks of treatment, nearly 1 in 2 patients in the upper GI and more than 1 in 3 in the lower GI achieved polyp burden reductions of ≥65%. Two patients achieved ≥98% reductions in upper GI polyp burden. Substantial reductions in larger, higher-risk polyps : Six of eight patients with polyps >5 mm at baseline had reductions in the number of these polyps after 12 weeks of treatment. Four achieved reductions of ≥80%, including two whose larger-polyp counts fell from more than 90 polyps to one. No new safety signals observed: Favorable chronic dosing safety profile, consistent with the MEK inhibitor class. The highest-grade treatment-related adverse event (TRAE) was Grade 1 or 2 in 21 of 26 patients (81%) and Grade 3 in four patients (15%); one patient experienced no TRAEs. No Grade 4 or 5 TRAEs were reported. No additional discontinuations were reported since the previous data cutoff. Registrational trial: The Company anticipates initiating a registrational trial in the second half of 2027, pending ongoing FDA discussions, and will provide additional details later this year. Denver, Colorado , Nov. 02, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Recursion (Nasdaq: RXRX), a leading clinical-stage company pioneering AI-enabled drug discovery and development, today announced new positive Phase 2 data from the ongoing TUPELO trial of REC-4881, an investigational, oral MEK1/2 inhibitor for familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP). The new analyses show that most patients had reductions in both the number of larger, higher-risk polyps and in lower GI polyp burden, building on the upper GI results announced on October 15, 2026 . Together, these findings support the potential of REC-4881 as an oral therapy to address FAP across the GI tract. Lisa Boardman , M.D., a gastroenterologist and Professor of Medicine at Mayo Clinic , presented the results in a Presidential Plenary at the Collaborative Group of the Americas on Inherited Gastrointestinal Cancer (CGA-IGC) Annual Meeting in Denver, Colorado . “People have been doing research in the chemoprevention space in FAP for decades, and at least in the United States , we still don’t have an agent that is FDA approved. We’re still having to send FAP patients for major surgeries and we’re still doing frequent scopes on these patients. The need for effective chemoprevention in FAP is very large, and it’s only going to increase over time as the number of FAP patients continues to increase,” said Bryson Katona , M.D., Ph.D., Director of the GI Cancer Genetics Program, University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine , and TUPELO study investigator. “We recently shared data that showed deep, durable reductions in polyps with REC-4881, particularly in the upper GI, where patients with FAP face the greatest risk and the fewest options. Today's update goes a layer deeper. REC-4881 is reducing the larger polyps that often drive much of the surgery for these patients, across the GI tract from a single oral therapy,” said Najat Khan , Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Recursion. “This is a lifelong disease with no approved pharmacologic therapies, and REC-4881 is the clearest proof point yet of what we built Recursion to do. Our priority now is to align with the FDA on a registrational path and move with focus and discipline toward a trial in the second half of 2027.” Latest Data from Phase 2 Trial of REC-4881 Deep reductions in total polyp burden, sustained off treatment The TUPELO study was designed to study polyp burden reduction after 12 weeks on REC-4881 (4 mg QD) and again after 12 weeks off-treatment. Results show a rapid and durable treatment effect across the GI tract. Trial results have strengthened since the November 2025 data cut, including expanded adult FAP population ages 18 years and older: 87% of patients (13 of 15) had a reduction in total polyp burden after 12 weeks of treatment, with a 47% median reduction.
